root_idea.summary: A root centered on disturbance, agitation, and violent or unstable motion.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from causing something to move or shake, through becoming agitated or moving to and fro, to descriptions of quivering bodies, turbid liquids, weakness, confused sound, and figurative confusion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form rather than the passive inflected Quranic surface form.
Displayed separately as the Quran-attested verbal noun.

senses.definition: To shake or convulse violently; to put into violent motion.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive: the earth is violently convulsed or shaken.
In the Quranic construction رُجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ رَجًّا, the verbal noun specifies the violent convulsion of the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mare: to be near foaling, with the parts on either side of the tail quivering or quaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV usage applied to a mare near delivery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become agitated, convulsed, shaken, or quivering; to move to and fro.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage said of the sea and other things, and also of flesh or bodily parts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confused or unclear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage said of darkness or speech; confused speech may be conflicting or unintelligible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatigue, weariness, or weakness accompanied by tottering or unsteadiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An independently reported meaning of رَجْرَجَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A confused, murmuring, or rumbling sound, including the mingled voices of a company or the sound of thunder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also describe a rumbling sound heard from the chest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of confusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage meaning being in confusion or disorder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of commotion, agitation, convulsion, shaking, quaking, or quivering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a condition of disturbance rather than the causative act of shaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak or emaciated; applied to livestock and camels, and to men who are weak or lacking understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical application includes weak sheep, goats, camels, and men; the association with lack of intelligence is stated specifically for men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The covert or retreat of a lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for the lion’s hiding place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel with a large hump, possibly one with a large quivering or shaking hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The interpretation involving a quivering hump is reported with uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quivering, agitated, convulsed, or moving to and fro.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet for something in such a state; the feminine رَجْرَاجَةٌ is applied to a woman or girl whose flesh or hind part quivers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slaver or drivel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for saliva or fluid issuing from the mouth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fluid associated with the gelatinous substance called qaris, a preparation made from fish and similar materials.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a specialized lexical equivalence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Crumbled or broken bread softened with grease or gravy; also a dish of such softened bread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A culinary noun describing a soft, compact preparation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate plant name recorded under this headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Residual water in a trough or tank, turbid and mixed with mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes stagnant or remaining water in its receptacle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water mixed with slaver or drivel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized meaning for a liquid mixture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spittle or saliva issuing from the mouth, especially flowing saliva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-fluid usage distinct from water mixed with saliva.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large company or troop in war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for a numerous military group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People characterized as unintelligent, base, vile, corrupt, or of the lowest social sort.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective characterization of a people or party; the semantic range includes those lacking understanding and those regarded as morally bad or mean.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an army or troop: agitated to and fro in its march and scarcely advancing because of its multitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of a very numerous troop whose movement is crowded and sluggish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain well-known medicine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dish or mess of the food called fālūdh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized culinary usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Characterized by a confusion of voices caused by a multitude of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a place or situation filled with numerous confused voices.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Core causative shaking and the Quranic earth construction.
Specialized Form IV usage of a mare near foaling.
Intransitive agitation, quivering, and movement to and fro.
Nominal state of commotion or shaking.
Weakness or emaciation in animals and men.
She-camel with a large, possibly quivering hump.
Epithet for something quivering or agitated.
Unintelligent, base, corrupt, or low people.
Feminine application to a woman or girl whose flesh quivers is covered under the related epithet.
Numerous army or troop moving with agitation and little progress.
Confusion of voices caused by a multitude.

cautions: The interpretation of رَجَّاءُ as specifically referring to a quivering hump is reported as uncertain.
